name: Categories Status
author: Chetan Vaghela

sections.description:
Categories Status lets you assign a Draft status to taxonomy terms, allowing you to temporarily hide them from the frontend without permanently deleting them.

Instead of deleting categories, tags, or custom taxonomy terms that may be needed again in the future, simply change their status to Draft. Draft terms remain available in the WordPress admin and can be restored at any time by changing their status back.

This plugin is especially useful for websites with frequently changing categories, seasonal content, product classifications, or custom taxonomies.

Features

  • Add a Draft status to selected taxonomies.
  • Hide draft taxonomy terms from the frontend.
  • Keep taxonomy terms safely stored in the WordPress admin.
  • Restore draft terms at any time without recreating them.
  • Supports custom taxonomies.
  • Lightweight and easy to configure.
  • Simple integration with the WordPress admin.

Use Cases

  • Temporarily disable categories without deleting them.
  • Hide seasonal product categories.
  • Archive taxonomy terms for future use.
  • Manage custom taxonomy terms more efficiently.
  • Prevent accidental loss of taxonomy data.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install it through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Open CV Categories Status from the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Select the taxonomies you want to support.
  5. Save your settings.
  6. You can now change supported taxonomy terms between Published and Draft.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin delete taxonomy terms?

No. The plugin never deletes terms. It only changes their status to Draft, allowing them to be restored later.

Does it support custom taxonomies?

Yes. You can enable the Draft status for supported custom taxonomies.

Can I restore a draft term?

Yes. Simply change its status back from Draft to make it visible on the frontend again.

Does this affect existing posts?

No. The plugin only controls the visibility of taxonomy terms and does not modify your posts or their content.
